description_en: In 1907 CE (1962 VS), the Sataḥ was constructed by the five sons of Bhāgavatabhakta Māhemā to fulfill his wish for the building.The Sataḥ is located at Kājī steps (ghāṭa) on the bank of Bagmati river. According to L. Śākya (NS 1122, p.28), the name of the place reverts to Kājī Bhāgavatabhakta Māthemā building it. The Sataḥ architecture incorporates various elements from Nepali architectural style. The ground floor features a phalcā with five bays. The upper floor consists of a Newarī window (sãjhyā) in Rana style with open spaces between the turrets. Though the Sataḥ bears the resemblance from buildings of Malla era, it possesses a unique architectural style.Kājī Bhāgavatbhakta had made a commitment to establish the Rādhākṛṣṇa temple (KAT2710) along with this Sataḥ. Before his demise, he had allocated 20murīs paddy, 1murī10pāṭhī(9 ropanī-s, 12ānā) of land for the annual conduct of rituals of both Sataḥ and Temple. But he could not personally complete the commitment. To fulfill his wish, Bhāgavatbhakta Māthemā's five sons finalised the construction of the buildings. An inscription attached to a wall in the Sataḥ records that in the event of reconstruction, any descendant of Sardāra Haribhakta Māthema is entrusted with the responsibility of rebuilding it. To prevent the loss or sale of lands an inscription containing the list of land allocated for the Sataḥ was made and placed on the wall of the Sataḥ in 1951 CE (2008 VS).The Sataḥ served as a residential space for a long period of time. Even the terrace was used as a room. The terracotta tiles (jhiṃgaṭī) from the roof were replaced by iron roofing sheets. After the earthquake of 2015 CE (2072 VS) the Sataḥ had been heavily damaged, leading to the evacuation of the residence. Subsequently it was reconstructed with the assistance of the Integrated Development of the Bagmati Civilization, a project under Nepal Government's Ministry of Urban Development, in collaboration with a loan from the Asian Development Bank. The new Sataḥ was inaugurated in October 2022 CE (2079 VS).Every year on the occassion of Kṛṣṇaṣṭamī descendants of Bhāgavatabhakta Māthemā perform annual worship of the Kṛṣṇa Temple. The ritual arrangements and distribution of the gifts tot he deity take place in the phalcā of the Sataḥ. In the past, devotees used to stay awake the whole night, offering prayers, something no longer in practice. On the day of Bālā Caturdaśī the Jyāpu community from Naradevi would come together to construct a wooden bridge (Bātcālã) in front of the sataḥ by the Bagmati river, only to be later dismantled. For this occasion, members would sacrifice a buffalo sacrificed in the phalcā of the Sataḥ. This ritual is no longer practiced. Likewise, the tradition of holy men (sādhus) residing in the phalcā during Rāma Navamī and Śivarātrī is no longer practiced (local resident, Mahrjana, male, age 57).The sataḥ served as a residence for a long period of time. Even, the terrace of the sataḥ was used as a room by replacing the terracotta tiles (jhiṃgaṭī) from the roof with iron roofing sheets. After the earthquake of 2015 CE (2072 VS), the sataḥ suffered a severe damage, leading to the evacuation of the residence inside, and it was subsequently reconstructed. The reconstruction of the sataḥ was carried out with the assistance of the Integrated Development of the Bagmati Civilization, a project under Nepal Government's Ministry of Urban Development, in collaboration with a loan from the Asian Development Bank. The sataḥ was inaugurated in October 2022 CE (2079 VS) after completing its reconstruction.Every year on the occassion of Kṛṣṇaṣṭamī descendants of Bhāgavatabhakta Māthemā performs annual ritual of Kṛṣṇa Mandira. The ritual arrangements and distribution of the deity's gifts take place in the phalcā of the sataḥ. In the past, devotees used to stay awake the whole night, offering prayers, which is no longer in practice. On the day of Bālā Caturdaśī, there was a tradition where the Jyāpu community from Naradevi would come together to construct Bātcālã (a wooden bridge) at the front of the sataḥ on the Bagmati River, and later they would dismantle the temporary bridge. For this occasion, they would partake in a feast with a buffalo sacrificed on the phalcā of the sataḥ, but this tradition is also no longer practiced. Likewise, the tradition of holy men (sādhus) residing on the phalcā of the sataḥ during Rāma Navamī and Śivarātrī is also no longer practiced (local resident, Mahrjana, male, age 57).
description_ne: यो सतः विसं १९६२ (सन् १९०५) मा पाँच दाजुभाई मिली पिता भागवतभक्त माथेमाको इच्छालाई पूर्णता दिन निर्माण गरेको हो ।बागमती किनारस्थित काजी घाटमा यो सतः बनेको छ । काजी भागवतभक्त माथेमाले बनाएको घाट भएकाले यो स्थान कालान्तरमा "काजी घाट" कहलिएको हो (L. Śākya NS 1122, p.28) । निर्माता भागवतभक्तको नामसँग जोडेर उक्त घाटलाई "भगवतेश्वर घाट" पनि भनिएको पाइन्छ भने माथेमा खलकको पूर्वजले बनाएको सतः भएकाले "माथेमा सतः" पनि भन्ने र लेख्ने गरिएको पाइन्छ (Pruscha 1975, K-271, p.93) । बागमतीतिर मोहोडा पारी बनाइएको सतः परम्परागत नेपाली वास्तुमा केही परिवर्तन ल्याई बनाइएको छ। भूमि तलामा पाँच कवलको फल्चा बनाइएको छ र मथिल्लो तलामा खुला कोठा निकाली मोहोडा भागमा सँझ्याः हालिएको छ । माथिल्लो तलाको दायाँ-बायाँ आयताकार दुई टावर (कोट/पुर?) उठाइएको छ । मल्लकालीन दरबारका चौकोट जस्ता देखिने यस्तो वास्तु अन्य सतःहरूमा पाइँदैन । सतःमाथिको मध्य भाग कौशीको रूपमा खुला छाडिएको छ जसलाई राणाकालीन वास्तुको प्रभावका रूपमा बुझ्न सकिन्छ । यो सतः विसं १९६२ (सन् १९०५) मा काजी भागवतभक्त माथेमाको मनोकांक्षास्वरूप उनका पाँच छोराबाट निर्माण भएको हो । भागवतभक्त माथेमाका पिता सरदार हरिभक्त माथेमा तत्कालीन नेपालभाषाका भक्ति भावका कविता लेख्ने कवि थिए । नेपालमा राणा शासन अन्त गरी प्रजातन्त्र स्थापना गर्ने क्रममा शहीद भएका चार शहीदमध्येका धर्मभक्त माथेमा यिनै भागवतभक्त माथेमाका नाति थिए (L. Śākya NS 1122, p.17) । काजी भागवतभक्तले यस सत:सहित राधाकृष्ण मन्दिर (KAT2710) स्थापना गर्ने संकल्प गरेका थिए । सत: र मन्दिरमा नित्यपूजा लगायत अन्य वर्षकृत्यका खातिर २० मुरी धान, एक मुरी १० पाठी गहुँ आयस्ता आउने गरी कूल ९ रोपनी १२ आना खेत गुठी राख्ने संकल्प पनि उनीबाटै भएको थियो । उनको इच्छा पूर्ण हुन नपाउँदै विसं १९५४ (सन् १८९७) मा भागवतभक्तको मृत्यु भएको थियो । दिवंगत पिताको इच्छानुसार उनका पाँच छोराहरू सुब्बा वेदभक्त, सुब्बा आदीभक्त, सुब्बा लिलाभक्त, खरिदार हंशभक्त र खरिदार रत्नभक्त मिली यो सतः र राधाकृष्ण मन्दिर (KAT2710) निर्माण गरेका थिए । सतः निर्माण पश्चात् नित्यपूजा र कृष्णाष्टमीको दिनमा वर्षवर्द्धनपूजा गर्नुपर्ने व्यवस्था गरिएको थियो । सत: र मन्दिर भत्केमा सरदार हरिभक्त माथेमाका सन्तान जसले बनाए पनि हुने व्यवस्था गरिएको कुरा सतःमा प्राप्त अभिलेखमा उल्लेख छ । सत: र मन्दिर स्थापना गर्दा राखिएका जग्गाहरू हराउने सम्भावना भएको हुँदा जग्गाको अभिलेखीकरण गरी शिलापत्रमा कुँदी विसं २००८ (सन् १९५१) मा सतःभित्र शिलापत्र स्थापना गरिएको थियो ।सतः आवासका रूपमा लामो समयदेखि प्रगोगमा थियो । माथिल्लो तलाका झिंगटी हटाई जस्तापाताले छाई कौशीलाई पनि आवास कक्षकै रूपमा प्रयोग गरिएको स्थिति थियो । विसं २०७२ (सन् २०२५) को भूकम्पले सतःलाई क्षति पुर्याए पश्चात् यहाँका निवासीलाई हटाई सतःको पुनर्निमाण गरिएको हो । नेपाल सरकारको सहरी विकास मन्त्रालय अन्तर्तत अधिकार सम्पन्न वागमती सभ्यता एकिकृत विकास समितिद्वारा एशियाली बैंकको ऋण सयहोगमा सतःको पुनर्निर्माण समापन गरेको हो । विसं २०७९ (अक्टोबर २०२२ ) कार्तिक महिनामा सतःको पुनर्निर्माण कार्य सम्पन्न गरी उत्घाटन गरिएको थियो ।प्रत्येक वर्ष कृष्णाष्टमीको दिन भागवतभक्त माथेमाका सन्ततिहरू नजिकैको कृष्ण मन्दिरमा वर्षवर्द्धनपूजा गर्न हाजिर हुन्छन् । पूजाका क्रममा सामग्री व्यवस्थापन र पूजा पश्चात् प्रसाद ग्रहणका खातिर यस सतःको फल्चा प्रयोग हुने गर्दछ । विगत कृष्णाष्टमीमा रातभर जाग्राम बसी भजनकीर्तन गर्ने र प्रसाद वितरण गरी उल्लासपूर्ण ढङ्गले पर्व मनाउने गरिन्थ्यो जुन हाल लोप भैसकेको छ । नरदेवीका ज्यापु समुदाय बाला चतुर्दशीका दिन सतःको अग्र भागमा रहेको बागमतीमाबात्चालँ(काँठको पुल) बनाउन आउँदा र पछि भत्काउन आउँदा यस सतःको फल्चामा बसी राँगाको बलिसहित भोज खने चलन थियो तर यो थिति पनि लोप भैसकेको छ । रामनवमी र शिवरात्रीमा भारतबाट बाबाजिहरू आई सतःको फल्चामा बस्ने थिति पनि लोप भैसकोको छ (local resident, Mahrjana, male, age 57) ।

historical_events.event_name: Establishment of the Sataḥ and Rādhākṛṣṇa Temple (KAT2710)
historical_events.event_description: The foundation of the Sataḥ and Rādhākṛṣṇa Temple was laid in honor of Bhāgavatabhakta Māthemā's commitment. Sardāra Haribhakta Māthemā, a poet who expressed his literary prowess in Nepalbhasa, was the father of Bhāgavatabhakta Māthemā. Among the four martyrs, Dharmabhakta Māthemā was Bhāgavatabhakta Māthemā's grandson (L. Śākya NS 1122, p.17). Kājī Bhāgavatbhakta, driven by his dedication, pledged to establish the Rādhākṛṣṇa temple (KAT2710) along with this Sataḥ. Despite his passing, he designated 20murīsof paddy and 1murī10pāṭhī(9ropanī-s, 12ānā) of land for the annual rituals of the Sataḥ and temple. He couldn't fulfill his commitment during his lifetime. In fulfillment of his wish, Bhāgavatbhakta Māthemā's five sons, named Subbā Vedabhakta, Subbā Ādībhakta, Subbā Lilābhakta, Kharidāra Haṃśabhakta, and Kharidāra Ratnabhakta, undertook the construction of both the Sataḥ and the Rādhakṛṣṇa temple (KAT2710).

In 1951 CE (2008 VS), an inscription was affixed to the Sataḥ's wall, outlining allocated lands for the Sataḥ. This measure was taken to prevent the loss of these lands. Following the Sataḥ's completion in the early 20th century, provisions were established for daily rituals and an annual observance on Kṛṣṇaṣṭamī. This inscription bears testament that any descendant of Sardāra Haribhakta Māthema carries the responsibility of its future restoration.

In the aftermath of the 2015 CE earthquake, the Sataḥ encountered extensive damage, necessitating the evacuation of its inhabitants and eventual reconstruction, which concluded by 2022 CE. This revival of the Sataḥ was facilitated through the collaborative efforts of the Integrated Development of the Bagmati Civilization project, an initiative under Nepal Government's Ministry of Urban Development, along with financial support from the Asian Development Bank. The Sataḥ's refurbishment was successfully accomplished, culminating in its inauguration in October 2022 CE (2079 VS).
A stone name plate positioned above the main entrance, although lacking a specific installation date, serves as an identifier for the location.
A metal name plate, denoting the alternative name "Māthemā Sattala" for Bhagvateśvara Ghāta Sataḥ, has been attached. However, no record of the installation date is present.
